wiki_catalogs.name: Project Overview
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create comprehensive content for the TBS LPDP Try Out project overview section. Explain the project's purpose as a free, browser-based practice testing platform for the Indonesian Tes Bakat Skolastik (TBS) exam administered by LPDP. Document its key features including timed section testing, server-authoritative grading, offline capabilities, and multi-platform support. Describe the architecture showing how Git question banks, Python generators, GitHub Pages SPA, Supabase backend, and Tauri desktop app work together. Include the exam format details with three subtests (verbal, quantitative, problem-solving), timing, and scoring system. Provide context about the project being independent and not affiliated with LPDP or PUSMENDIK. Use terminology consistent with the codebase and make it accessible to both beginners and experienced developers.

# TBS LPDP Try Out - Comprehensive Project Analysis

## 1. Project Introduction

### Purpose Statement
TBS LPDP Try Out is a free, browser-based practice testing platform for the Indonesian **Tes Bakat Skolastik (TBS)** exam administered by LPDP (Lembaga Pengelola Dana Pendidikan). The application replicates the timed, section-by-section Computer-Based Test (CBT) experience provided by PUSMENDIK, offering students comprehensive preparation tools with scoring, answer reviews, and detailed explanations for every option.

### Core Goals and Objectives
- **Authentic Exam Simulation**: Reproduce the exact timing and structure of the official LPDP TBS examination
- **Comprehensive Practice Material**: Provide 480 questions across three subtests in eight complete packages
- **Secure Assessment**: Server-authoritative grading with answer-key protection to prevent cheating
- **Progress Tracking**: Save attempts, provide detailed analytics, and enable revision tracking
- **Accessibility**: Available as both web application and offline desktop/mobile apps

### Target Audience
- Indonesian students preparing for LPDP scholarship examinations
- Educational institutions offering test preparation services
- Self-motivated learners seeking structured practice for standardized testing

## 2. Technical Architecture

The project follows a modern full-stack architecture with clear separation between frontend, backend, and data layers:

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Client Browser/App] --> B[React SPA + Vite]
    B --> C[Supabase Backend]
    C --> D[(PostgreSQL Database)]
    C --> E[Edge Functions]
    C --> F[Storage Service]
    
    G[Question Bank Generator] --> H[Git Repository]
    H --> I[GitHub Pages Deployment]
    H --> J[Offline App Distribution]
    
    K[Tauri Desktop App] --> L[Local Exam Engine]
    M[Android App] --> N[Mobile Exam Experience]
```

### Component Breakdown

**Frontend Layer (React + TypeScript)**
- Single Page Application built with React 18 and Vite
- Hash-based routing for GitHub Pages compatibility
- Responsive design supporting web and mobile devices
- Offline capability through Tauri wrapper

**Backend Layer (Supabase)**
- PostgreSQL database with Row Level Security (RLS)
- Real-time capabilities and authentication
- Edge functions for server-side processing
- Storage service for question images and assets

**Data Management**
- Git-versioned question bank with JSON schema validation
- Python-based question generation and validation tools
- Immutable published releases for version control

### Design Patterns

**Repository Pattern**: Question data is managed through a centralized repository system that abstracts data sources (local vs remote)

**Strategy Pattern**: Different exam modes (web vs offline) are implemented through interchangeable strategies

**Observer Pattern**: Real-time updates for exam progress and status changes

**Factory Pattern**: Dynamic creation of exam sections and question types

### System Relationships

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant WebApp
    participant Supabase
    participant Database
    
    User->>WebApp: Start Exam
    WebApp->>Supabase: Create Attempt
    Supabase->>Database: Insert attempt record
    Database-->>Supabase: Confirmation
    Supabase-->>WebApp: Attempt ID
    
    WebApp->>Supabase: Load Questions
    Supabase->>Database: Fetch from published release
    Database-->>Supabase: Question data
    Supabase-->>WebApp: Questions with RLS applied
    
    User->>WebApp: Submit Answers
    WebApp->>Supabase: Grade via RPC
    Supabase->>Database: Calculate score securely
    Database-->>Supabase: Graded result
    Supabase-->>WebApp: Final score
```

## 3. Key Implementation

### Main Entry Points

**Application Bootstrap** (`web/src/main.tsx`)
- React application initialization
- Router configuration and global state setup
- Environment-specific configuration loading

**Root Component** (`web/src/App.tsx`)
- Route management using React Router
- Authentication and maintenance gates
- Platform detection for web vs offline app behavior

### Core Modules

**Exam Engine** (`web/src/pages/AttemptPage.tsx`, `web/src/pages/ExamPage.tsx`)
- Timed exam execution with countdown timers
- Section navigation and progress tracking
- Answer persistence and auto-save functionality
- Auto-submission on timeout handling

**Question Management** (`web/src/lib/bankSource.ts`, `web/src/lib/bankSchema.ts`)
- Abstracted question source abstraction (local vs remote)
- JSON schema validation for question integrity
- Asset loading and caching mechanisms

**State Management** (`web/src/contexts/MaintenanceContext.ts`)
- Global application state management
- Maintenance mode coordination
- Feature flag handling

### Configuration Approach

**Environment Configuration** (`web/src/lib/config.ts`)
- Build-time environment variable injection
- Platform-specific feature toggles
- API endpoint configuration

**Build Configuration** (`vite.config.ts`)
- Development and production build optimization
- Code splitting and lazy loading
- Asset bundling and optimization

### External Dependencies

**Core Framework Dependencies** (`web/package.json`)
- React 18 for UI components
- React Router for navigation
- Supabase client for backend communication
- Tauri plugins for desktop/mobile capabilities

**Development Dependencies**
- TypeScript for type safety
- Vite for fast development and building
- Testing utilities and tooling

### Integration Points

**Supabase Integration** (`web/src/lib/supabase.ts`)
- Database connection and authentication
- Real-time subscriptions
- Storage operations

**Email Service Integration** (`supabase/functions/question-report-digest/index.ts`)
- Automated report generation and delivery
- Resend.com email service integration
- Error handling and retry logic

**Version Control Integration**
- GitHub Actions for automated deployment
- Semantic versioning with automated bump scripts
- Release artifact generation

### Component Relationship Diagrams

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[App Component] --> B[Route Guards]
    B --> C[HomePage]
    B --> D[AttemptPage]
    B --> E[ReviewPage]
    
    D --> F[ExamEngine]
    D --> G[TimerComponent]
    D --> H[AnswerTracker]
    
    F --> I[QuestionRenderer]
    F --> J[SectionNavigator]
    
    K[SupabaseService] --> L[Authentication]
    K --> M[DatabaseOps]
    K --> N[StorageOps]
```

## 4. Key Features

### Functionality Overview

**Multi-Format Exam Delivery**
- Web-based exam taking with responsive design
- Offline desktop application using Tauri
- Android mobile application support
- Consistent experience across all platforms

**Advanced Question Types**
- Verbal reasoning (synonyms, antonyms, analogies, syllogisms)
- Quantitative reasoning (arithmetic, algebra, number sequences)
- Problem solving (data sufficiency, combinatorial probability)
- Reading comprehension with passages and data interpretation

**Security and Integrity**
- Server-side answer key storage and grading
- Row Level Security for data isolation
- Turnstile CAPTCHA integration for abuse prevention
- Immutable published releases preventing tampering

### Implementation Highlights

**Real-time Collaboration** (`web/src/hooks/useTick.ts`)
- Synchronized timer functionality across components
- WebSocket-based real-time updates
- Graceful error handling for network interruptions

**Performance Optimization** (`web/vite/bank-reader.ts`)
- Lazy loading of question banks
- Efficient memory management for large datasets
- Caching strategies for improved performance

**Error Handling and Recovery** (`web/src/components/MaintenanceGate.tsx`)
- Graceful degradation during maintenance periods
- Automatic retry mechanisms
- User-friendly error messages and recovery options

### Feature Architecture Diagrams

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Idle
    Idle --> SelectingPackage: Choose Exam
    SelectingPackage --> StartingExam: Begin Test
    StartingExam --> InProgress: Timer Started
    InProgress --> ReviewMode: Complete Section
    InProgress --> Timeout: Time Expired
    ReviewMode --> SelectingPackage: Next Package
    Timeout --> SelectingPackage: Retry Option
    SelectingPackage --> [*]: Exit
    
    note right of InProgress
        Real-time saving
        Progress tracking
        Timer countdown
    end note
```

**Quality Assurance Pipeline**
- Automated question validation using JSON Schema
- Python-based test generation and verification
- Continuous integration with automated testing
- Manual review workflow for content quality

**Analytics and Reporting**
- Performance metrics collection
- Question difficulty analysis
- Student progress tracking
- Automated report generation and distribution
